clue.text: Thumb stuck in awkward sod by government officials

indicators.note: one name is wedged inside the other, as if stuck into it

parts.note: a cuss is a cantankerous, awkward person
Tom Thumb, the thumb-sized hero of the folk tale

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a tiny person has been jammed in by bureaucrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thumb' looks like a verb, but it is the first name of the fairy-tale Tom Thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs is the government service whose officers check goods at the border.

clue.text: Top ministers getting together — for display purposes only?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the senior ministers of a government meeting as a body
second meaning: a glass-fronted piece of furniture for showing off ornaments

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark jokes that the senior ministers are mere ornaments on show.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the body of senior government ministers and a piece of furniture with shelves for showing objects.

clue.text: Exhibitionist who's pissed with hippy mate

indicators.note: drunk, so the letters of these words stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
'man' is the hippy's form of address, as in 'cool, man'

explanation.surface: A show-off turns up drunk with a long-haired friend in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: A showman is someone who loves performing and drawing attention, an exhibitionist by temperament.

clue.text: Those getting on live date during Pope Leo's tour

indicators.note: the two letters come in the middle of the touring letters, within their span
on a tour the pope goes round, so his name's letters go round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L marks the live terminal on a British three-pin plug
D, the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: The pensioners mark the date of a papal visit, which is live on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: On a British plug the terminals are labelled L (live), N (neutral) and E (earth).
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly people are said to be getting on, meaning advancing in years.

clue.text: Good to get away from Glenda's coarse material

indicators.note: the letter for good leaves the surname, departing from it

parts.note: Glenda Slagg is the spoof gossip columnist of Private Eye, so her surname is meant

explanation.surface: A goody-goody flees from Private Eye's vulgar columnist and her crude stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Glenda Slagg is Private Eye's long-running parody of a brash tabloid columnist.
explanation.definitionFit: Slag is the rough stony waste left over from smelting ore, a coarse material.

clue.text: Lang whipped with tie of member

indicators.note: beaten into a new shape, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Lang is flogged, with a tie involved somewhere below the belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Genital means relating to the sex organs, the 'member' in its anatomical slang sense.

clue.text: Guys do bugger off!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Guy Fawkes effigies are stuffed with straw or rags before Bonfire Night
second meaning: a rude command to go away

explanation.walkthrough: A guy is the effigy British children stuff and burn on Bonfire Night, 5 November.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes what is done to a guy, and as an exclamation it is a rude dismissal, like telling someone to get lost.

clue.text: Someone with a far from active sexual partner

definitions.text: Someone with a far from active
definitions.meaning: reads as a lover with a lazy partner; the partner is in fact dead, about as inactive as can be
the person on the other side is a corpse

explanation.walkthrough: The understatement 'far from active' suggests a dull bedfellow, but the partner is lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A necrophiliac is sexually attracted to corpses, whose partners are as passive as possible.

clue.text: Slut, popular one, who used to score a lot

definitions.text: who used to score a lot

parts.note: tart is slang for a promiscuous woman
in, as in fashionable
the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A promiscuous favourite is remembered for having lots of lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' means to have sex in the surface, but to write music in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Tartini was an 18th-century Italian violinist and composer who wrote a great deal of music.

clue.text: City sees one with zip undone entering member

indicators.note: the group of letters goes into the limb

parts.note: a leg is a limb, one of the body's members

indicators.note: a zip that is undone comes apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in town notices a man with his flies open and his member making an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Leipzig is a major city in eastern Germany, in Saxony.

clue.text: See 23
Get a load of that soldier, one of several sniffing round Brenda

definitions.text: one of several sniffing round Brenda

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise or admiration
GI, an American soldier

explanation.surface: A leering soldier is one of a pack of men pursuing a woman called Brenda.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, who kept many corgis.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a Welsh dog breed, famous as the late Queen's pets trailing around her.

clue.text: Eye 's vital statistics not so sensitive? Smashing!

definitions.note: an activity defined by the figures it handles, a loose fit

parts.note: more numb, so number in the sense of having less feeling
crunching, breaking with a grinding noise

explanation.surface: A joke about the magazine's measurements being made less tender and then delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' here is numb with -er, not a figure: the solver must hear it as 'more numb'.
explanation.definitionFit: Number crunching is the heavy processing of figures and data, the work of producing statistics.

clue.text: Resort of most devious putter-up of Aitken

indicators.note: taking a crooked route, so the letters of the word wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Jonathan Aitken, a Tory minister, stayed at the Paris Ritz in 1993; who paid the bill led to his downfall

explanation.surface: A holiday spot is chosen by the craftiest person who hosted a disgraced politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Aitken lost a libel case over the Ritz bill and was jailed for perjury in 1999.
explanation.definitionFit: St Moritz is a fashionable Swiss ski resort in the Engadine valley.

clue.text: Horny thing on Underground line — regularly laid in farmer's field!

parts.note: a corn is a patch of hard, horny skin on the foot
the Circle line of the London Underground

explanation.surface: A randy creature on the Tube is said to be bedded often out in the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid' teases a sexual meaning, but it is flattened crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn circles are rings of flattened crops that keep appearing in fields, often made by hoaxers.

clue.text: Blair's not finished getting high on speed

definitions.note: the answer is a speed of 100 miles per hour, so the fit is loose

indicators.note: the name loses its last letter, left incomplete

parts.note: Tony Blair, the Prime Minister when the puzzle appeared
up, as in raised

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister is said to be stoned on amphetamines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' looks like the drug but means velocity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ton-up is British slang for doing a hundred miles an hour, especially on a motorbike.

clue.text: In bad taste? Well, that's kids!

parts.note: off, as in gone bad or out of order
a spring is a natural well of water

explanation.surface: A parent shrugs off a crude remark: that is just how children are.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's children, and kids is the informal word for children.

clue.text: See 23
Tit for tat Secretary of State conceals measure on backing for example

indicators.note: the surname hides the other letters inside it

parts.note: Cyrus Vance, US Secretary of State under President Carter
en, a printer's measure of width

indicators.note: the abbreviation is read in reverse, backed up

explanation.surface: A minister retaliates and hides a measuring device in support of an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Vengeance is retaliation for a wrong, the same idea as tit for tat.

clue.text: A tourist needs six flipping lives and balls lifted

parts.note: the Roman numeral VI

indicators.note: the short word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: is, as in exists

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: rot, both slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: A tourist needs half a dozen exciting holidays and nonsense brushed aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is someone who comes to see a place, which is what a tourist does.

clue.text: On rising, does a Brenda — so anything goes

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word rising is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
what Brenda, Private Eye's name for the Queen, does: she rules

explanation.surface: Getting up, someone imitates the Queen, and anything is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: No rules means there are no restrictions at all, the situation where anything goes.

clue.text: Drink an afterthought for such Northerners

parts.note: lap, as a cat does milk
PS, a postscript added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A drink as an afterthought suits northern folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapps, now usually called Sami, are people of the far north of Scandinavia.

clue.text: See 6
Gag about hiding in barn was penetrative

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are concealed inside the farm building

parts.note: a shed is a farm outbuilding like a barn

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gagged victim concealed in a barn suggests something sinister went on.
explanation.definitionFit: Shagged is British slang for had sex with, the act in which one partner penetrates.

clue.text: Brenda involved in ma's hip replacement — heavenly creatures!

indicators.note: being involved in something means being inside it
a replacement suggests the letters are put back in a different order

parts.note: Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda, and ER is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: The Queen gets caught up in Mum's hip operation, surrounded by angels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' rearranges MAS HIP into SAPHIM, and ER goes inside after S. Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphim are the highest order of angels, beings of heaven.

clue.text: Rave about managing the country air — it makes many people switch off

definitions.text: it makes many people switch off

parts.note: a rave is a big dance party
to air is to broadcast
political, concerned with government

explanation.surface: A rant on governing the nation, aired on TV, sends viewers to the off button.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads PARTY POLITICAL BROADCAST: PARTY fills 23 Down, POLITICAL 16 Down and BROADCAST 9 Across, so the lights' number order scrambles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Party political broadcasts are TV slots given to parties, notorious for prompting viewers to turn off.

clue.text: Tit roughly grabbed by one US city's rampaging leader

indicators.note: the jumbled bird is seized and held inside

parts.note: a, the indefinite article
LA, Los Angeles

indicators.note: the letters are handled roughly and come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small bird is roughly grabbed by a rioting leader of an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila the Hun led his armies on destructive rampages across fifth-century Europe.

clue.text: City-backed politician, an arse

indicators.note: read backwards, in reverse

parts.note: Ur, the ancient city of Mesopotamia
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician backed by the City is dismissed as an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arse' in the surface is an insult; in the answer it is the backside itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump is the hindquarters, an animal's backside, so slang for a person's behind.

clue.text: Some old-style Republican, revolting type

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, a run hidden inside them

parts.note: the name runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned Republican is labelled a disgusting sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 in England, a famous rebel.

clue.text: See 11
About to dash to do what Blair did to Labour

definitions.text: do what Blair did to Labour

parts.note: re, as in regarding
style, flair or panache

explanation.surface: Blair is about to rush off and give the party his treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a verb of hurrying but is the noun for flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Blair rebranded the party as New Labour, giving it a new style and image.

clue.text: Kept a vigilant watch on filth with Dettol initially

parts.note: the filth is British slang for the police

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the brand name is taken

parts.note: the brand of disinfectant supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone guarded the dirt carefully, armed with disinfectant at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Dettol is a British brand of disinfectant, which suits the 'filth' surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To police an area is to keep order there by close supervision, a vigilant watch.
